item.title: College football recruiting: 10 prospects on flip alert before signing day
item.description: Big-name prospects flipping during the early signing period has become less common over the years, but the days leading up to it tell a different story. Coaches aren't only focused on closing out the regular season; they're also making last-minute pitches to players or scheduling last-minute visits to make one final impression. The top players in the country are already committed to their respective programs, but that doesn't mean that they're locked in until they've signed on the dotted line. Who are some of the biggest names to watch heading into the early signing period? More: 2028 football recruiting rankings: USA TODAY Sports' updated top 100 Here are 10 football recruits we're keeping an eye on for possible flip alerts: 5-star DL Jalen Brewster: Texas Tech to LSU No one has been a bigger star in the 2027 recruiting cycle than Brewster, and he's been a long-time commit to Texas Tech, committing to the Red Raiders last October. Now at Buford (GA), while he hasn't locked down his commitment to Texas Tech, that hasn't stopped other programs from taking their shots at him. He remained steadfast in his commitment to Texas Tech even after visits to Florida, LSU, Texas and SMU. The rumor mill once again began to swirl when Brewster showed up in Baton Rouge for LSU's game against Texas on Nov. 14. Nothing has seemingly come from that visit, though, and he's scheduled to return to Lubbock on Thanksgiving for the Red Raiders game against TCU. Other schools have tried, but Texas Tech hasn't given the cycle's top prospect any reason to flip away from his long-time commitment. Prediction: Texas Tech 5-star TE Ahmad Hudson: LSU to Nebraska A five-star in both football and basketball, Hudson was a massive win for LSU on both fronts when he announced his commitment back on May 3. However, Nebraska has remained a constant thorn in the Tigers' side throughout Hudson's recruitment and, at times, has looked like it was in a good spot to flip him. Nebraska wanted to get Hudson back to Lincoln this weekend for its game against Ohio State, but he's instead focusing on a second-round playoff game. That decision not to go could work wonders for LSU. He's visited Baton Rouge every time, and not heading back to Lincoln could be a massive win for Lane Kiffin. Prediction: LSU 5-star LB Kaden Henderson: Texas A&M to Notre Dame At one point, it appeared like Texas A&M would run away with the top class in the 2027 cycle with more than 10 five-star commitments. That's cooled off a lot as the season has progressed; A&M has struggled, and numerous flips have occurred. Back in June, the Aggies landed a massive win over Notre Dame when Henderson chose Texas A&M over the Fighting Irish. That loss then did not slow down Marcus Freeman, who has remained a constant in Henderson's recruitment. item.title: Ryan Clark says Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished because it was ‘never built on character’
item.description: Credit: The Pivot, ESPN The final act of Aaron Rodgers’ career took a pretty shocking turn this week. The future Hall of Famer was unceremoniously benched via a social media post late Tuesday night with little explanation. In response, he showed up on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and threw his longtime coach Mike McCarthy under the bus, accusing him of falling asleep in meetings and several other shortcomings in his first year in Pittsburgh. We’ve seen great players leave the league far from their peak. Tom Brady got his last Super Bowl with the Buccaneers, but his final season in Tampa Bay was far from pretty. But nothing in that final season affected Brady’s status amongst the all-time greats. Given Rodgers’ exit was so loud, and according to many former pros , so against the unwritten rules of football life , will Rodgers see his reputation take a hit due to how this chapter ends? Ryan Clark doesn’t think so. Speaking on his show The Pivot , Clark, who has been public with his feelings about Rodgers for some time, argued that the quarterback’s legacy as a player was safe, because it was never tied to him being a good guy. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy is in no way tarnished, because his legacy was never built on character,” Clark said. “If Tom Brady says this when leaving the New England Patriots, we’re shocked. We’re surprised. Because it’s against everything he’s ever shown us. Mike McCarthy should’ve known that kissing a rattlesnake was safer than coaching Aaron Rodgers again. He’s shown many times there’s no loyalty, there’s nothing I won’t say, I won’t think about the person I’m talking about before I think about myself. Many people will say that he fell on the sword. That this was about the team. Well, you’re already out of the building. This is about you.” Clark noted that the fact that Rodgers’ former teammates were forced to answer so many questions about his departure was proof that his actions weren’t about helping the team. “Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that to be some sort of martyr. Aaron Rodgers did that because he got demoted and said, ‘Oh, I’m going to get you way more than you could get me.'” From there, Clark lamented what has become of his former team , arguing that he was against the hiring of McCarthy in the first place as it went against what the Steelers usually looked for in a coach. “Aaron Rodgers’ legacy isn’t tarnished, because it was never built on character” Multiple things can be true at once. Aaron Rodgers can be both right & wrong. Telling the truth doesn’t preclude you from being disingenuous, & Mike McCarthy can have a winning record while operating like a bad head coach. Regardless of where you stand, one thing is fundamentally clear: The Pittsburgh Steelers have a problem so deeply rooted that they may need to tear it all down to fix it. @thepivotsports on @thepivot @youtube #ThePivotSports #ThePivot #Steelers #AaronRodgers https://t.co/1j2kEwzC58 — Ryan Clark (@Realrclark25) November 27, 2026 Clark ultimately come

item.title: Bears Week 12 Flashbacks: Arrowhead Upset, Hester’s Magic, Turkey Day
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 25: Cairo Santos #2 of the Chicago Bears lines up a field goal attempt in the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on November 25, 2021 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s edition of the Gridiron Time Machine, we’re revisiting an unlikely comeback at Arrowhead, a valuable lesson in why you should never kick to Devin Hester, and a Thanksgiving victory that came down to the final second. So hop aboard the time machine for another fantastic trip down memory lane. 1.) 1993, Bears @ Chiefs: An unlikely comeback at Arrowhead November 21, 1993 | Bears win 19-17 The Bears entered Week 12 of the 1993 season with a 4-5 record under first-year head coach Dave Wannstedt. A trip to Arrowhead Stadium to face the 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs wasn’t exactly the ideal opportunity to get back to .500. Things certainly didn’t look promising early on, as future Hall of Fame running back Marcus Allen found the end zone twice to give Kansas City a 14-0 lead in the second quarter. The Bears managed to get on the board before halftime thanks to a pair of Kevin Butler field goals from 32 and 45 yards out, cutting the deficit to eight. Chicago continued chipping away in the third quarter when Tim Worley broke loose for a 25-yard touchdown run. A blocked extra point kept the Bears from pulling within one, and a Nick Lowery field goal extended Kansas City’s lead to 17-12 heading into the fourth quarter. If you were expecting Jim Harbaugh to lead some sort of aerial assault to complete the comeback, think again. Harbaugh completed 13 of his 20 pass attempts for just 98 yards and two interceptions, finishing the afternoon with a passer rating of 37.1. He was considerably more effective with his legs, rushing for 56 yards on eight attempts. The Bears leaned heavily on their ground game, rushing for 185 yards on 43 attempts. Worley led the way with 59 yards, while Neal Anderson added another 42. With just over three minutes remaining, Anderson punched it in from one yard out to give Chicago its first lead of the afternoon. The Bears’ defense, which recorded five sacks and held Kansas City to just three second-half points, made sure that lead stuck. The Chiefs would go on to win the AFC West and reach the AFC Championship Game that season, but on this particular Sunday, the Bears had their number. Winning on the road against one of the AFC’s best teams without throwing for 100 yards? That’s some Chicago Bears football right there. 2.) 2007, Bears vs. Broncos: Denver learns not to kick to Hester November 25, 2007 | Bears win 37-34 (OT) Coming off their Super Bowl appearance the previous season, the 2007 Chicago Bears found themselves sitting at 4-6 entering Week 12. While the season hadn’t gone according to plan, the Bears still had one of the most electrifying players in football at their disposal. item.title: Big Blue View mailbag: Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy, playoffs, more
item.description: Michael Buscemi asks: Really curious about this question and answer at least in every game there is a few times a cornerback or safety drops an interception do they ever have drills for defensive backs from quarterbacks that train their hands better to catch and making deceptions it happened so often I’m just curious to see what your answer is about practicing drills to help control the ball. Ed says: Michael, these guys are at the highest level of their sport. They practice catching the ball every day — or at least every day there is a practice. There are always drills that involve catching the ball, both standing still and on the move. There is also a JUGS machine guys can use at the end of practice. Several players use it all the time. Reality is, though, game and practice conditions are much different. You practice the fundamentals of catching so that it becomes muscle memory, but you can’t mimic game speed or circumstances. John Steinbreder asks: As is the case with so many Giants fans, I am enjoying every part of the Jameis Winston Experience and the deft and very selfless ways he has been performing his duties as QB2 for the Giants. And that has me wondering: has there ever been a back-up quite like him? The thoughtful mentoring of the young signal callers. Coming in off the bench when needed to win games. And now his role as the man orchestrating the tush-push, whether as a runner or passer. Then, of course, there are the signals he actually calls, in part to try and draw the opposing team offsides and also to entertain. And his barking, “Who Let The Dogs Out” in the Commanders game still has me chortling weeks later. I am also curious as to your thoughts on Harbaugh utilizing Jameis in those situations as a way of protecting JJ from taking unnecessary shots. It makes me think back to Tom Coughlin who never called QB sneaks with Eli because he did not want to expose him unnecessarily to injury. It’s a pretty smart move on Harbaugh’s part, to protect JJ and also to keep Jameis engaged and involved. Ed says: John, there have been many veteran backup quarterbacks over the years who have willingly helped younger players learn their craft. There have been backups/journeymen with flamboyant personalities like Ryan Fitzpatrick. Winston, though, is one of a kind. He willingly embraced helping Jaxson Dart. Even after J.J. McCarthy was given his starting job, Winston has embraced doing everything he can to help McCarthy and the team as a whole. This guy is a team captain, a member of the team’s leadership council and the guy who breaks down the team’s pre-game on-field huddle. I don’t know of a backup quarterback who has carried that kind of respect from his teammates. As for the QB sneak stuff, I think there are two parts to it. I think it is something that Winston does well — not all quarterbacks have the feel for it, or really want to throw themselves into that scrum. item.title: Scaling the Rocks: Kyle Freeland goes the distance
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - AUGUST 02: Kyle Freeland #21 of the Colorado Rockies looks on after his first career complete game win in a game against the Kansas City Royals at Coors Field on August 02, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kyle Cooper/Colorado Rockies/Getty Images) Good morning, Purple Row! Here’s what’s going on with the Colorado Rockies and the rest of Major League Baseball. 2026 Rockies Individual Performance of the Year I thought there was a real possibility that Cole Carrigg would take home his third consecutive Purple Row Award, but Kyle Freeland earned a rather convincing victory with 52% of the vote for his complete game against the Kansas City Royals on August 2 . On one of the hottest afternoons in Coors Field history, with the trade deadline looming the following day, Freeland took the mound for his 251st career start. There was a feeling it could be his last start in a Rockies uniform, but Freeland seemed unperturbed. The veteran southpaw gave Royals leadoff hitter Carter Jensen four different looks to open the game, putting him away with a knuckle curve. View Link The Royals scratched across their only run of the afternoon in the second inning when Luke Maile followed a John Rave single and a Josh Rojas walk with a two-out RBI single. Kansas City threatened again in the third when Jac Caglianone doubled with one out. Freeland moved the ball around the zone against Salvador Perez before burying consecutive knuckle curves, getting the veteran catcher to chase the second on a full count. View Link He retired Starling Marte on the very next pitch. Kansas City wouldn’t have another baserunner until the ninth. Freeland leaned into his cutter and sinker, inducing weak contact, and wasn’t shy about doubling up on his knuckle curve. He took different approaches against Maile and Jensen in the fifth, but put both away with consecutive curves before giving Nick Loftin five different looks and inducing a harmless fly ball. With the Rockies clinging to a 2-1 lead in the sixth, Brett Sullivan successfully challenged a knuckle curve at the bottom of the zone to strike out Marte and end the inning. View Link The Rockies broke things open with a six-run sixth inning, and by then, Freeland was cruising. He dispatched the Royals on just eight pitches in the seventh, including a four-pitch strikeout of Tyler Tolbert. Zach Agnos began warming in the bullpen in the eighth, but Freeland retired the side in order once again. He had needed just 49 pitches to navigate five consecutive perfect innings. With 97 pitches under his belt, Freeland opened the ninth with his hardest pitch of the afternoon — a 92.4 mph fastball that Caglianone grounded to second. View Link It was the 18th consecutive batter Freeland had retired, a career high. A double from Perez and a single from Marte put runners on the corners with one out, and Agnos was warming once again. item.title: 3 Keys to Victory: Michigan Football at Ohio State
item.description: In the blink of an eye, Michigan’s season went from a complete and utter failure to what could be a similar story to the 2024 season. The Wolverines were 6-5 going into The Game in 2024, but the outlook on the season completely changed when it upset the No. 1 team in the country.Michigan’s 6-5 team of 2026 doesn’t have that exact same opportunity, but after beating then-No. 4 UCLA last week, it would feel similar if it capped the season off with a win over the Buckeyes. It’s the biggest game of the year, no matter the records or circumstances, as Michigan and Ohio State meet for the 122nd rendition of The Game. Here are the keys to victory for the Wolverines. Win the turnover margin Last week proved exactly why the turnover margin is so important in football, and how damaging it can be for a Michigan team that has struggled with that aspect of the game all season long. UCLA entered last Saturday with a +16 turnover margin, the best in the Big Ten and tied for second in the FBS. The Wolverines forced three turnovers and only turned it over once — the final takeaway leading to a game-altering touchdown at the beginning of the fourth quarter. Michigan is still last in the Big Ten with a -8 turnover margin, but Ohio State isn’t great either with a -3 turnover margin, tied for 14th in the conference. If it needs reminding, three of the Wolverines’ biggest wins — Week 2 against Oklahoma, Week 7 against Penn State, Week 11 against UCLA — have been the only games they won the turnover margin. One of the only faults of this Michigan defense has been its inability to force turnovers, but if last week was an indication of how The Game will go, it could be a long day for an Ohio State offense that has turned the ball over seven times in the last four games, three of which ended in losses. Keep a strong run game Freshman running back Savion Hiter had himself a game against the Bruins. For an offense that’s been struggling to find its footing all season long, especially in the run game, his performance proved something replicable. Hiter had a career-high 26 carries for 104 yards against UCLA, and it was his second consecutive game with more than 100 yards rushing. Ohio State has the 15th -best rushing defense in FBS, allowing just 100.3 yards per game. Even with the injuries and blunders of the Buckeyes’ offense, the defense has remained intact and hasn’t allowed more than 116 yards rushing to an opponent in the last four weeks, despite three of them ending in losses. If the Michigan offense can limit the negative run plays caused by blocking issues along the line, and rally behind Hiter and the run game to spark the offense, it may score just enough points to win. Continue making field goals The unsung heroes of Michigan’s win over UCLA was freshman kicker Jacob Baggett and punter Cam Brown, the latter of whom handled some difficult snaps as the holder. item.title: Final Audition: 3 fixes Michael Penix needs to save his Falcons future
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warms up on the sideline during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix exits the Week 11 bye and enters a seven-game stretch that could define his career. With scrutiny mounting , the final two months of 2026 will not only dictate whether Penix remains the Falcons’ starter entering 2027, but could also determine whether he ever gets another shot to lead an NFL franchise. To save his job, Penix must show immediate growth in three critical areas: starting faster, surviving pocket pressure, and rediscovering his signature deep ball. Penix must fix his first-quarter freeze According to Next Gen Stats , the Falcons’ slow starts have been fueled by a 31st-ranked first-quarter EPA per play and 32nd-ranked first-quarter passing yards. Leaning on the run game would help, with Atlanta’s early-game run rate plummeting from 56 percent in Penix’s first three starts to the 24th-ranked 42 percent over the last five. But the Falcons cannot ask star running back Bijan Robinson to carry the entire offense, as Penix has to pull some weight. Per NFL.com , Penix has completed 46 percent of his throws in the first quarter while averaging just 3 yards per attempt. The Falcons have produced just six passing first downs in the first quarter in Penix’s eight starts, compared with an NFL average of 19. This keeps the team from sustaining offense, thanks to a league-low first-quarter third-down efficiency of 10 percent across Penix’s starts. This isn’t a problem unique to 2026, as Penix posted a dismal 38.8 passer rating in the first quarter during his rookie season before surging to 108.8 in his second. That leap offers hope that more time in Tommy Rees’ offense can spark a similar turnaround. But as a third-year pro, Penix’s early-game struggles are harder to excuse, and Atlanta cannot afford to wait until 2027 for competence. Pressure is Penix’s kryptonite While the slow starts are problematic, they at least show growth potential. However, Penix’s biggest issue is his inability to handle pressure. Rarely do quarterbacks thrive under pressure, but few struggle as much as Penix. Per Next Gen Stats , Penix’s completion percentage over expected (CPOE) plummets by a league-worst 13 percentage points when pressured. Remarkably, the chasm between Penix and the NFL’s second-worst passer under pressure (Jameis Winston) is just as wide as the gap between Winston and the next eight quarterbacks on the list. Penix’s struggles against pressure are in a tier of their own. PFF’s marks on Penix under pressure are even more stark. And then the question becomes “for how long?” and we can only hope that the answer to that question is “weeks” rather than “months” or even “seasons.” But that’s putting the cart ahead of the horse. item.title: Rain, wind gusts up to 30 mph expected for 49ers-Seahawks showdown
item.description: Rain falls during the fourth quarter of an NFC Divisional Playoffs game between the Green Bay Packers and the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Jan. 20, 2024. (Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Sunday's pivotal matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks is set to be played in wet and windy weather . In a phone interview with SFGATE on Friday, National Weather Service meteorologist Dial Hoang said rain is expected to hit the Bay Area on Sunday morning. The rain will likely roll in from the North Bay, where it's expected to arrive shortly after sunrise, and reach Santa Clara County and the area surrounding Levi's Stadium in the late morning. Once it arrives, it won't go away for the rest of the day, he said. "We're looking at the rain continuing across the Bay Area during the game, and especially after the game," Hoang told SFGATE. "Those lingering showers may extend into Monday morning." It shouldn't be overly cold - the forecast calls for temperatures to be in the mid-60s - and shouldn't rain too heavily, with around a quarter of an inch expected. But Hoang said it will be "gusty" during Sunday's game, with wind gusts expected to be between 25 and 30 mph. "It does look like the wind is going to be a strong factor," Hoang said. It's been a wet few weeks in the Bay Area, with a Nov. 18 storm breaking rainfall records in various Bay Area cities and causing flooding in several pockets of San Francisco. The region also saw near-historic high tides last week as part of the ongoing impact of El Niño this winter. The 49ers have already made several preparations in anticipation of a rainy winter. While the players and coaches were training in Colorado Springs, Colorado, to prepare for a game in Mexico City last week, the 49ers built a rain canopy over one of their practice fields in Santa Clara. Why does this now exist at #49ers HQ? Kyle Shanahan: "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something" https://t.co/dh4iWI49Mk - Harrison Rich (@harrisonrich_) November 25, 2026 When asked during a news conference why the team opted to add the canopy, head coach Kyle Shanahan quipped, "Because I keep getting told about El Niño or something," before explaining its benefits, which can give the 49ers the closest thing to the bubble-like indoor facilities that many football teams have across the country. "Sometimes, when it's just like a monsoon out there and we're playing in a bubble, you can get a little bit more done with not being in that [rain]," Shanahan said. "So, if it ends up being like that, like people have warned, it's nice that at least we can walk through and stuff like that." It was sunny at the Niners' practice on Friday in Santa Clara, but the team is practicing with the rain in mind. With starting quarterback Brock Purdy out with an ankle injury, backup Mac Jones was spotted squirting water onto the football to help practice throwing a "wet ball," similar to what the team is expecting on Sunday.

item.title: UH's 'Old Man Club' prepares for final home game after 15 combined college football seasons
item.description: Brandon Mack II's eight-year college odyssey comes to an end with UH on Saturday. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) They've heard all the jokes about their age, how long they've played college football and all the changes they've witnessed. Meet defensive linemen Brandon Mack II and Quindario Lee, card-carrying members of the University of Houston' s unofficial "Old Man Club." When the No. 18 Cougars host Baylor for Senior Night on Saturday, two of the longest-tenured players in school history will play their final home game. Eight seasons for Mack. Seven seasons for Lee. UH vs. BAYLOR: How to watch "A lot of stories with those guys, a lot of memories," said James Ross III, the Cougars' edges and defensive run-game coordinator. Both are 25 years old. Mack goes by the nickname "Unc." Lee, who is three months older, is called "Gramps." "B-Mac always reminds me I'm older," Lee said with a laugh. And you'll likely never see their type of longevity again. The NCAA's new age-based eligibility model, which limits players to five seasons within a five-year window, will make it impossible to replicate careers that have combined for 15 seasons and spanned two presidential terms. "I'm just excited to see them transition into life," Ross said. He jokingly added, "We tried to find some more years. There are no more hidden years anywhere else." Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . While there is no official category, Mack and Lee are believed to be the longest-tenured players in program history. Their careers have been prolonged by an extra year of eligibility because of the COVID-19 pandemic and medical redshirts. A three-star defensive end out of high school, Mack signed with Ole Miss in 2018. He spent four seasons in Oxford, missing one with a foot injury, before transferring to UH in 2023. His first season with the Cougars ended prematurely, however, when he suffered a high-grade tear of the lat muscle on his left side in the second week of the season. He has been healthy the past three seasons, playing in 12 games in 2024 and set to play 13 games in consecutive seasons with the Cougars qualifying for a bowl. "I feel like yesterday was my first time in TDECU Stadium when we played UTSA and wore our powder blue jerseys," said Mack, who has posted 10 sacks over the past three seasons. "Then you blink and it's over. It definitely felt like it went by fast." Mack thought his college career was over last November. He began filling out information for the Cougars' Senior Night ceremony when he was told he had another year of eligibility. Lee's path has been just as winding. A three-year defensive lineman, Lee went from small-town Alabama to Fort Scott (Kan.) Community College. He transferred to Central Michigan, where he played 24 games over three seasons, before arriving at UH in 2024.

item.title: Panthers vs Buccaneers: Matchups to watch
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 25: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Bucky Irving (7) begins the celebration after scoring a touchdown during an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers on October 25, 2026 at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have a chance to plant themselves firmly in the drivers seat of the NFC South. They have a two game lead over every other team in the division, and right now the Buccaneers are the only team that have a chance to take the head to head tiebreaker over them. Taking a three game lead over the Bucs while also clinching not being on the wrong side of any head to head tiebreakers almost seems insurmountable given how hard it is for NFC South teams to win any games. That said, the last time these teams played was a complete catastrophe for the Panthers. They squandered away the home leg of the home-and-home with a performance featuring mistakes by every unit. They practically invented ways for things to go wrong, all the while they couldn’t stop either Buccaneers running back from gaining like 10 yards before making an attempt at tackling them. That first meeting is going to provide us with a little bit of a guide for where we’ll focus this matchups post. Panthers front seven vs Bucky Irving Bucky Irving has always been a nightmare for the Panthers. He averages over 100 rushing yards per game against Carolina for his career. The first meeting was no different. He finished with 106 yards on 24 carries, but that somewhat undersells how badly the Panthers struggled with him. He gained yardage on virtually every carry; he just didn’t have any long enough gains to boost his yards per carry. He’s had a couple of those games this year and is sneakily fourth in the NFL in rushing yards. The Panthers have to do a much better job of clogging up his run lanes and wrapping him before he has a chance to get into space, where he becomes nearly impossible to get down with just one guy. Panthers interior offensive line vs Vita Vea and Calijah Kancey The Panthers have had their issues blocking for Bryce Young up front. Luke Fortner has been a weak spot at center and Robert Hunt hasn’t been his old self. Vita Vea and Calijah Kancey are both top 20 in ESPN’s pass rush win rate for defensive tackles. They’re part of a Tampa Bay defense that’s becoming a very formidable unit as the season goes on. Young obviously has problems with interior pressure given his short stature. A night of Vea and Kancey disrupting the middle of the pocket is going to make it very hard for the Panthers offense to move the ball. They’re going to need Fortner and Hunt to step up and play better than they have to this point in the season. item.title: Space in Macy’s 100 Thanksgiving Day parades
item.description: null The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is sure to be a blast, but it is a bit light on "space." According to previews provided by the department store chain, the founder of the New York City holiday celebration, space fans turning up or tuning in to catch sight of an astronaut or other nod to NASA will have only a returning rocket to look forward to on Saturday (Nov. 28). (The parade has been postponed two days from Thursday, Nov. 26, due to bad weather.) Not that Macy's (or the space agency) has hinted about anything cosmic planned for the 100th parade; it's only that the event has had a long history of celebrating space exploration with its floats and balloons. "For our 100th parade, we're creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country," said Sharon Otterman, Macy's chief marketing officer, in a statement . First held in 1924 for Macy's colleagues, their friends and families, the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been held every year with the exception of a three-year break during World War II. Spanning longer than the dawn of the Space Age, the space race and NASA's entire 68-year history, the celebration has integrated space themes into its displays, even before the first rocket flew beyond Earth's atmosphere . Weighty weightless man The earliest space-themed feature of the parade may have been the "Space Ship," a float that made its first appearance in the 19th procession in 1945 and in various configurations — with and without astronauts and planets — appeared on and off through 1962. Perhaps more memorable, though, and certainly much larger, was the "Spaceman" (or, more appropriately, "The Giant Spaceman"). The 70-foot-long (21-meter) helium balloon made its debut in 1952, nine years before the Soviet Union's Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space. Described by Macy's as an "artist's conception of a visitor from another planet," the humanoid figure had a black spacesuit , a silver helmet and boots, a jet propulsion backpack and a black rocket gun. Once the heaviest balloon in the parade, the "Spaceman" was created by the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company years before anyone had entered space. (Image credit: Macy's) Ironically, for a figure garbed for the weightless environment of space, the Spaceman was for a long time the parade's heaviest giant balloon. At 600 pounds (272 kilograms), it was only tied by the Pink Panther in 1988 and then exceeded two years later by Bart Simpson. The rubber Spaceman was created by Goodyear Tire, the same company that contributed hardware to NASA's Apollo program , including the wire mesh non-pneumatic tires for the lunar roving vehicle. The Spaceman survived being torn when it was caught with a lamppost in 1955, and a helium shortage resulting in it and other balloons being filled with air and held up by cranes in 1958. It was retired after its seventh appearance in 1959, and ultimately was destroyed. 'The First Men on the

item.title: Ultramarathoner Who Ran Over 3,000 Miles in 41 Days Says He ‘Encountered Almost Dying Every Day’ (Exclusive)
item.description: Cameron Balser running Credit: Alessandro Portante NEED TO KNOW Cameron Balser broke the Trans America Run record, running 3,000 miles in 41 days across 12 states Balser faced physical, mental, and safety challenges, including traffic dangers and running up to 16 hours daily He credits his support team and community for helping him achieve his goal and inspire others through his journey After 41 days and over 3,000 miles, ultramarathoner Cameron Balser reached New York City Hall to set a new record for the Trans America Run on Friday, Nov. 20. Eight years in the making, Balser, 35, hoped to beat the previous record set by Pete Kostelnick, who ran from San Francisco City Hall to N.Y.C. in 42 days in 2016. The determined athlete was able to do so, beating Kostelnick by 13 hours and 45 minutes. Following the feat, Balser, 35, opened up to PEOPLE about what the run means to him, what some of the hardest parts were and how he leaned on Kostelnick to keep himself grounded in why he wanted to take this on in the first place. “Running’s always been something I’ve been very passionate about. I just didn’t know where that was gonna go. I ran some more ultramarathons and I met Pete, who had the record, and got to talk to him about his trip across the country,” Balser says. “That influenced me to want to run around America. In 2023, I ran the perimeter of the United States. I did a solo thing and I ran 11,170 miles in 294 days around America. After that, it kinda gave me a good resume for people to wanna kinda back me.” Cameron Balser running across America Credit: Alessandro Portante For the Trans America Run, Balser was sponsored by Mount to Coast . He started his race in San Francisco on Saturday, Oct. 10 before crossing 12 states over 41 consecutive days, climbing more than 42,000 meters and averaging 72.1 miles per day. Some days, he spent up to 16 hours running. “The team would wake me up around 4:25, 4:30. I would wake up then and have 10 minutes to slam some food and try to wake myself up. By 5:00 a.m. almost every day, we would start running,” Balser says. Every five miles, he says he would “eat literally as much as I could.” “Then I would go back out there and the team would be looking for anything that would need water, food and stuff like that. Running from 5:00 a.m. to basically 9:00 p.m. every night and then 10 minutes I would have a little bit of a wind down and then I would go to sleep and I did that for basically 41 days straight,” Balser reflects. Prior to the run, Balser worked on a regenerative farm and got used to the long hours. After the farm work, he would run 25 to 30 miles a week, and then on weekends would run 40 to 50 miles. “I was more prepared than I thought. We were very lucky and fortunate that it literally felt like miracle after miracle was unfolding in front of us,” Balser says. item.title: Luka Doncic accuses courtside fan of pushing him during heated wristband incident
item.description: Luka Doncic accuses courtside fan of pushing him during heated wristband incident originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic had a rough Friday night in San Antonio. The Los Angeles Lakers lost 99-96 to the San Antonio Spurs , dropping their season record to 15-4. The loss also knocked Los Angeles out of the NBA Cup. Things got even worse for Doncic after the final buzzer. As he walked toward the tunnel at the Frost Bank Center, he got into an argument with a fan sitting near the walkway. Video from the arena showed Doncic tossing his wristband to a female fan. A moment later, he heard she did not want it. Doncic walked back to pick it up and the man sitting next to her returned it before shoving the Slovenian star in the back. Doncic turned around right away to confront the man. Lakers forward Jarred Vanderbilt and arena security quickly stepped in to separate them. After the game, Doncic spoke to reporters about what happened. He blamed the fan for starting the physical contact. "I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else," Doncic said . Luka Doncic on the altercation with a fan: "I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn't want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else." https://t.co/aCfOCG7iEt — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 28, 2026 Many fans on social media did not believe his side of the story. Several users noted that the video made it look like Doncic threw the band out of anger after a tough loss. Los Angeles controlled the game early on. The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the first half and went into halftime ahead 54-38. Everything changed in the third quarter. San Antonio outscored Los Angeles 30-14 to get right back into the game. Doncic played 39 minutes and finished with 31 points, eight assists, six rebounds, and three steals. He struggled badly from deep, making just 1 of his 13 shots from 3-point range. Austin Reaves added 21 points for the Lakers, and Walker Kessler finished with 10 points and 13 rebounds. Stephon Castle led the Spurs with 26 points. Victor Wembanyama added 25 points and 16 rebounds to help San Antonio complete the comeback. item.title: Alabama Gets Unexpected Iron Bowl News as Auburn Makes Last-Minute Changes
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer looks on against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama’s final regular-season game suddenly has another storyline, and the latest developments could affect Saturday night’s Iron Bowl. Auburn released an updated SEC availability report Friday night, revealing significant changes involving two of its most important players. One development provides the Tigers with a major boost ahead of their trip to Bryant-Denny Stadium. However, the other leaves Auburn without a key defensive contributor against the Crimson Tide. With Alabama’s College Football Playoff positioning at stake, both updates could become important Saturday. Auburn Receives Major Quarterback Update Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown was upgraded from questionable to probable on Friday’s SEC availability report. The designation represents an encouraging development after Brown appeared on the injury report earlier in the week. According to On3’s Pete Nakos, Brown is expected to start Saturday against Alabama. However, his availability will not be finalized until the SEC releases its final pregame report. Brown has been one of Auburn’s most productive offensive players this season. The senior has completed 65.6% of his passes for 2,035 yards, 15 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Additionally, he has rushed for 644 yards and nine touchdowns. His dual-threat ability provides Auburn with another dimension against Alabama’s defense. Another Auburn Star Receives Disappointing News While Brown’s status improved, linebacker De’Marcus Riddick received a less encouraging update. Riddick was downgraded from questionable to out Friday night. The Auburn defender has been dealing with an ankle injury that has prevented him from returning to action. His absence could become particularly important against Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Russell has demonstrated the ability to extend plays with his legs, forcing opposing defenses to account for his mobility. Without Riddick, Auburn will need other defenders to assume additional responsibilities. The Tigers will also be without linebacker Bryce Deas and cornerback Gavin Jenkins. Consequently, Auburn enters the rivalry with several important defensive absences. Alabama Also Faces Injury Concerns Alabama has dealt with its own injury challenges entering the Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide listed seven players as out on Friday’s SEC availability report. Those players include offensive lineman Casey Poe, linebacker Cayden Jones, defensive lineman Jeremiah Beaman and tight end Josh Ford. Defensive backs Jireh Edwards and Nick Sherman also remain unavailable. Meanwhile, linebacker Caleb Woodson and defensive lineman Devan Thompkins were listed as probable. item.title: GB v Spain schedule, order of play and how to watch Davis Cup semi-final
item.description: Great Britain face Spain for a place in their first Davis Cup final since 2015, with Arthur Fery needing to beat Carlos Alcaraz in the singles. Leon Smith’s side stunned Germany in the quarter-finals on Thursday after doubles pair Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the decider . Great Britain have not been in the Davis Cup final since Andy Murray led the team to its first title of the Open era 11 years ago. Alcaraz sat out Spain’s quarter-final win over Austria as he nurses a hamstring injury after winning the ATP Finals last weekend. Spain are the favourites to win the Davis Cup with two top-10 singles players in their line-up, in Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar. Jodar got Spain off to a winning start, overcoming the British No 2 Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 in the opening rubber. The winner of the semi-final in Bologna will play hosts and defending champions Italy, after they overcame Czechia. Here’s everything you need to know How to watch Davis Cup The semi-final against Spain will be shown on the BBC Sport website and BBC iPlayer, with the tie starting at 11am BST (12pm local time). Order of play From 11am Singles 1: Rafael Jodar bt Cameron Norrie 6-2 7-5 Followed by Singles 2: Arthur Fery v Carlos Alcaraz (If required) Doubles: Patten/Skupski v Martinez/Granollers Preview: Fery backed to ‘take risks’ in ‘free hit’ Leon Smith has told Arthur Fery to have no regrets if he gets the chance to play Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals. Great Britain’s upset win over Germany in Bologna on Thursday set up a mouth-watering clash with Spain as Smith’s side bid to reach the final for the first time since claiming the title in 2015. Fery will be playing just his fourth match in the competition but is set to face the World No 1 and No 3 back-to-back after losing to Alexander Zverev on Thursday. Alcaraz sat out Spain’s quarter-final win over Austria having won the ATP Finals last weekend despite nursing knee and hamstring issues but it would be a surprise if he did not play singles – and potentially doubles – on Saturday. Spain captain David Ferrer was keeping his cards close to his chest, saying: “I will see on Saturday. I don’t know yet. But it could be possible.” Mixing in such circles is another indication of Fery’s meteoric rise this season, and he was clearly disappointed not to be able to threaten Zverev. Arthur Fery will take on Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals (Getty) Smith said: “I think it’s another chance for him to go out and see what it feels like, then figure out ways that he can actually hurt Carlos. “The more matches he gets at this level, which is still very, very new for him… I think embrace it, don’t be scared of it. “People hate hearing this ‘free hit’ thing. It kind of is. Just go out, express yourself. Don’t come off the court with any regrets. Try to play safe in any way? No. Go and play. Go and take some risks. Shot make. Enjoy it.” Fery has not taken a set off Zverev in three meetings but this will be his first chance

item.title: “I’m Just like Shaq Free-Throw Shooting-Wise” – Victor Wembanyama Humbly Admits to Struggling at the Line As Lakers Legend Catches Stray
item.description: Shaquille O'Neal, Victor Wembanyama © X/ @Lakers, @spurs San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama admitted he was struggling at the free-throw line and compared himself to Los Angeles Lakers legend Shaquille O’Neal. Wembanyama missed five of his eight attempts at the line in Friday’s 99-96 win over the Lakers, including a crucial one up-three with 57 seconds left. Stephon Castle saved Wembanyama by knocking down a 3 and giving the Spurs a six-point lead. Wembanyama missed another free throw up two with just over two seconds left, but made his final attempt that sealed the Spurs’ win. Dissecting his underwhelming display at the charity stripe, Wembanyama told Prime Video analysts he was like O’Neal at the free-throw line. “I gotta say, I’m just like Shaq free-throw shooting-wise right now,” he said. O’Neal was one of the worst free-throw shooters in the league, and teams often fouled him in the clutch because of it. O’Neal was often benched when opponents played the foul game while trailing in close games. The Lakers legend shot 52.7% from the free-throw line. Wembanyama is much better over his career. Entering Friday’s game, he was a career 81.3% free-throw shooter and 77.8% on the season. Although it’s a career-low mark, Wembanyama is still one of the better shooting bigs in the NBA from the free-throw line. Victor Wembanyama’s elite rebounding allows Spurs to complete comeback win over Lakers Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs trailed by 20 points in the first half. However, they crawled back in the second half, inspired by Wembanyama’s elite two-way display. After managing only eight points and five rebounds in the first half, Wembanyama bounced back with 17 points and 11 rebounds in the second. His rebounding was decisive in that stretch. The Lakers won the 50-50 battles in the first half, but once Wembanyama locked in, there wasn’t much Los Angeles could do to stop the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Wembanyama finished with 25 points, 16 rebounds, four steals and two blocks, overcoming an inefficient shooting night with hustle and effort in other areas. Wembanyama may have also got the edge in the MVP race against rival Luka Doncic. While Doncic had the better scoring night with 31 points on 45.2% shooting, the loss, coupled with his decision-making in the momentum-swinging third quarter, could have tipped the scales. Wembanyama, on the other hand, played more efficiently, giving the Spurs a better chance to win. item.title: Detroit Lions’ playoff, NFC North odds still high despite loss to Bears
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions gives a speech in the team huddle prior to an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions’ loss to the Chicago Bears was deflating and disappointing. Not so much because it was a critical game for Detroit’s playoff odds, but because the Lions were in a prime position to win and take a stranglehold on the division. But as you’ll soon see, the Lions are still in a great position to accomplish everything in front of them. Let’s look at how their playoff, NFC North, and even Super Bowl odds have shifted after their Thanksgiving loss to the Bears. Postseason odds: NYT simulator: 78% (down 8%) RBSDM: 81% (down 4%) DVOA: 83.3% (down 6.3%) ESPN (FPI): 91.5% (down 5.5%) Even by the most pessimistic models, the Lions still have more than a 3-in-4 chance to make the postseason. Their loss to the Bears did not decrease their postseason odds by more than 10% across any of these four prediction models. ESPN still remains very high on the Lions, with a massive 91.5% chance to make the playoffs, but it seems like the more normal average is around 80-83%. NFC North title odds NYT simulator: 15% (down 14%) RBSDM: 20% (down 13%) DVOA: 19.3% (down 18%) ESPN (FPI): 30.6% (down 19.4%) Obviously, this loss had a bigger impact on Detroit’s chances to win the division, but the odds are not outstandingly long still. The Lions still have a 15-30% chance to win the NFC North, and that stands true because they still have three division games left. And while they’re all on the road, Detroit has proven they can go toe-to-toe with any of those teams. And the fact that Detroit has a 2-1 record in the division already gives them a nice leg up on the tiebreakers, as long as they continue to beat their divisional foes. NFC’s No. 1 seed NYT simulator: 4% (down 4%) RBSDM: 6% (down 6%) DVOA: 3.9% (down 6.3%) ESPN : 5% (down 6%) You can pretty much kiss the Lions’ odds for the No. 1 seed goodbye. Unless the San Francisco 49ers struggle down the stretch—and they do have tough games against the Seahawks, Giants, Rams, and Chiefs left—Detroit is not likely to finish any higher than the NFC’s No. 2 seed. Super Bowl appearance odds ESPN (FPI): 11.0% (down 1.9%) DVOA: 7.3% (down 3.1%) Surprisingly, the Lions’ Super Bowl odds have not been impacted too much. Perhaps their strong offensive performance against a decent Bears defense has fed the models’ optimism about Detroit being able to survive a shootout game. However, their defensive performance on Thursday looms large as well.

item.title: Red Sox Signing Brandon Lowe Would Hurt the Yankees Even More
item.description: Red Sox Signing Brandon Lowe Would Hurt the Yankees Even More originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox have spent this offseason trying to put themselves in a position to win the AL East, though so has every other team in the best division in baseball. Jazz Chisholm Jr. signing with the Blue Jays has only added to that. While the Yankees lost a good player and a rival in Toronto landed one, the Red Sox could be affected. Or, they could hurt the Yankees even more by signing Brandon Lowe. With Chisholm gone, the Yankees have a hole at second base, and Lowe seems like one option to fill it. Ultimately, this is the type of move that helps in more ways than one, as the Red Sox would improve their own lineup and take something away from their biggest rival. Lowe fits Boston's roster as a left-handed bat with big power who can play second base. Despite a somewhat crowded infield, the Red Sox’s offense is always looking for ways to improve. He has been an elite hitter when healthy, and any contending lineup could use more of that. While the Red Sox aren’t going to make a move just to impact the Yankees, it does raise questions about how much sense this would make. The only issue Boston might consider is that Lowe was also offered the qualifying offer, similar to Jake Bauers, who it already signed. Signing Lowe would cost the Red Sox more draft picks, though his 35-home-run production would make up for it. item.title: Aston Villa Starting XI vs Ipswich Town: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Aston Villa Starting XI vs Ipswich Town: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Aston Villa Predicted XI vs Ipswich Town as Unai Emery Eyes Reset at Portman Road Aston Villa head to Portman Road needing a correction, not another excuse. The recent run has been poor, the attacking output has been worse, and Unai Emery has decisions to make before facing Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich Town. The numbers tell the story. Villa had 55 per cent possession in the 1-0 defeat at RAMS Park and still failed to create a chance worth talking about. That is the issue. Possession without purpose is dead weight. Emery’s side have drifted into that trap across a damaging sequence of results against Fulham, Barcelona, Manchester United, Sunderland and Galatasaray. Saturday is not about style points. It is about restoring some basic attacking function. Defensive changes look likely Zion Suzuki is expected to keep his place in goal. In front of him, Villa may go back to experience and familiarity. Matty Cash could return at right-back, while Pau Torres may also come back into the side. That would be rough on Tyrone Mings and Taylor Harwood-Bellis, particularly after they combined for 15 defensive actions in midweek. Still, selection is not a reward scheme. Emery needs balance, and Torres offers cleaner progression from the back. Victor Lindelof should keep his place, and Ian Maatsen may continue on the left despite a zero per cent cross accuracy in the last match. It is not ideal, but Villa’s problems have gone well beyond one full-back’s delivery. Boubacar Kamara remains the obvious holding midfielder. Four defensive actions and four duel wins against Galatasaray underlined his value. He does the ugly work and, right now, Villa need someone doing it. Midfield tweak could sharpen Aston Villa Photo IMAGO The obvious midfield call is Ross Barkley for Joao Gomes. Villa have lacked progressive passing into the front line, and that matters when chance creation has become such a glaring weakness. Gomes brings industry, but the game is asking for more incision. Barkley is the logical fix if Emery wants cleaner progression through central areas. It is a practical change, not a glamorous one, but Villa need practical solutions. Attack needs movement and clarity Further forward, Ibrahim Mbaye could replace Alysson on the left after another ineffective display. If the aim is to inject directness, that switch makes sense. Photo IMAGO John McGinn may move out to the right, where his work rate and delivery tend to be more useful. Johan Manzambi could then shift into the central attacking role. He had little impact from the flank against Galatasaray, and the stat that stands out is brutal, he did not record a single touch in the opposition penalty area. Playing him centrally would at least put him nearer to Nicolas Jackson, who is expected to lead the line again. Jackson managed only one shot in the Champions League defeat. item.title: Ian Rapoport shares what he now knows about Brock Purdy’s ankle injury
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Brock Purdy recently suffered an ankle sprain but the quarterback’s injury is not expected to be a major problem. Purdy has put himself in the NFL MVP conversation this season en route to the San Francisco 49ers going 9-1. He has a 71.0 completion rate and the joint-second-highest average yards per pass (9.0) in the NFL right now, which is only bettered by Lamar Jackson (10.0 in five games). The 49ers will have to make do without Purdy against the Seattle Seahawks this weekend but it doesn’t appear as though the QB will be sidelined for too long. Brock Purdy’s injury not considered ‘major’ Speaking on the NFL Network this week, Ian Rapoport commented on the 26-year-old’s injury and said that it is ‘not considered to be major’. He stated: “Brock Purdy has not yet practised for the San Francisco 49ers. He’s dealing with an ankle sprain. It’s not considered to be major, but if a starting quarterback doesn’t practise at all, you don’t think he has a chance to play.” WebMD have previously reported that Grade 1 ankle sprains take around 1-3 weeks to recover from. Grade 2 could take 4-6 weeks and a Grade 3 could rule an NFL player out for ‘several months’. However, based on Rapoport’s comments saying Purdy’s issue is not ‘major’, it looks as though his problem would be classified in the Grade 1 category. After this week’s game with the Seahawks, the 49ers are next in action on December 6 against the New York Giants. They will then play the Los Angeles Rams on December 13 before clashing with the Los Angeles Chargers on December 17. Purdy could miss all three of those games if his injury recovery time is on the higher end of a Grade 1 sprain, but there is also a chance he could be back in a week’s time to face the Giants. item.title: 'I am not prepared': Rohit Sharma reveals how he agreed to return as Mumbai Indians captain
item.description: NEW DELHI: Veteran batter Rohit Sharma is back in charge of Mumbai Indians after a three-year hiatus, but the five-time IPL-winning captain says his return was not driven by a desire to reclaim the leadership role. It was the feeling that the franchise needed direction after a difficult few seasons. Rohit was on Friday reinstated as Mumbai Indians captain ahead of the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League. He will succeed Hardik Pandya, who has joined Punjab Kings in a trade involving pacer Arshdeep Singh. Rohit, who led Mumbai to five IPL titles, admitted that he was initially unsure about taking up the responsibility again. The decision came after discussions with the franchise management and some thought about the team's future. "My honest thought initially was, I am not prepared for this right now. I have to go back and think about it kyunki kaafi kuch ho chuka tha. Toh I don't know if I was in that frame of mind to do it or not," Rohit said in an interview. However, he eventually felt that the team needed someone to take it forward. "But then andar se feeling aisa aaya ki yaar I am not saying that this team needs me as a leader, but this team needs a direction right now. And whatever that direction is, if it is me, I am more than happy to drive this team forward," he added. 'That's not MI' Rohit's decision came against the backdrop of a disappointing run for Mumbai Indians. After winning the IPL in 2020, the franchise struggled to reproduce its earlier success. Mumbai finished fifth in 2021 and 10th in 2022 under Rohit. They reached Qualifier 2 in 2023 before the management decided to make a change in leadership, with Pandya replacing Rohit. The change did not bring the desired results either. Mumbai finished 10th in 2024, reached Qualifier 2 in 2025 and ended the 2026 season in ninth place. Rohit said the team's struggles had frustrated several players and made him reflect on how Mumbai could return to its old standards. "Look, I mean as soon as we finished the IPL, we had a very disappointing season and I was like not just me but many other players were quite frustrated with how we were playing," he said. "Main ghar gaya, I thought about it ki yaar it's not the team that used to be once upon a time. We need to get back to that. How can we do that? It happens to any team when you have seen such a high, there is bound to be a low." The 39-year-old was particularly concerned that Mumbai were not competing at the level expected of a franchise that had enjoyed so much success. "Disappointment qualification ka nahi hai. Disappointment tha ki hum theek se khel nahi rahe the. Jo responsibility the logon ke paas woh theek se ho nahi raha tha," he said. "Which again you know it's a very natural thing to happen. You know when you are losing, the momentum is not with you, the other teams are playing well, they are trying and capitalising more on you, putting pressure more on you and we were not responding to that pressure. item.title: 'An embarrassing figure!' - Roberto Mancini takes aim at Serie A clubs as Italy crisis forces drastic youth gamble
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Roberto Mancini has blasted Serie A's "embarrassing" lack of domestic talent after being forced to call up inexperienced teenagers for Italy's Nations League campaign. With the national side missing out on the quarter-finals, the head coach admitted he must take bold risks to rebuild the squad. Mancini turns to youth in Nations League Mancini has revealed that a shortage of domestic players in Serie A left him little option but to hand international call-ups to youngsters with minimal top-flight experience. Speaking in an interview with Corriere dello Sport , the Italy coach addressed his recent squad selections. Ahead of this month's Nations League fixtures, Mancini drafted several teenagers into the national team camp, including youth players Riccardo Cassano and Simone Lontani. The move came during a mixed international window for Italy, who defeated France before a 4-1 loss to Belgium ended their hopes of reaching the quarter-finals. 'Embarrassing' Serie A numbers force change At the heart of Mancini's frustration is the shrinking pool of eligible players competing regularly in Italy's top division. With domestic representation dropping sharply, the coach believes he must look beyond established club regulars to keep the national side competitive. "I was forced to (call up young players), given that the proportion of Italian players in Serie A has fallen to 30%. It's an embarrassing figure," Mancini admitted. "I have no choice but to seek out young players with potential who are capable of developing." Club indifference and a 20-year problem Italy's current struggles come against a sobering recent backdrop. Despite being four-time world champions, the national side have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups. Against Belgium, Mancini showed his willingness to trust emerging talent by handing an international debut to 20-year-old striker Alphadjo Cisse, who has scored ten goals for AC Milan this season. Mancini insists the structural issue is nothing new and expects no favours from domestic teams. "I have to take risks by fielding them in important matches," he said. "The clubs have no interest in the national team, which has to find its own solutions. There's no point in complaining about the situation that has existed for at least 20 years, we simply have to scout for players and give them experience, even if it means risking a few defeats." A long-term gamble for Italy's future With their Nations League campaign over at the group stage, Italy now face a defining period of transition. The national team will continue scouting emerging prospects and fast-tracking them into senior international football. Although this approach carries the risk of short-term setbacks, Italy clearly hopes that this early experience will ultimately pay off on the biggest stage.

item.title: Chad Johnson names the NFL team Aaron Rodgers could join immediately
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images What happens next to Aaron Rodgers is the question on the lips of a lot of people around the NFL, following what has certainly been a dramatic week. The 42-year-old quarterback will have likely watched his former team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, comfortably beat the Denver Broncos on Friday. It was the first game that Mike McCarthy’s team has played since Rodgers was released. A lot of damage has now been done to Rodgers’ reputation, which was already far from flawless, with teams across the league left considering whether bringing in the opinionated free agent quarterback is actually worth the risk. Chad Johnson thinks Aaron Rodgers could join the Denver Broncos Although the reality is that a change at quarterback for the Broncos is unlikely, Nix’s performance on Friday in Pittsburgh was one worthy of being benched by Sean Payton for the remainder of the season. “So, do you think the Broncos are going to try and make a change at the QB spot?” Joe Johnson asked on Nightcap. Shannon Sharpe: “No. No, they’ve got Jared Stidham behind him. Absolutely not.” Chad Johnson: “Hey, you know, Aaron Rodgers is right there, though.” Sharpe: “That ain’t happening. Boy, you think he’ll pull that with Sean Payton?” Johnson: “Aaron Rodgers, hold on. Aaron Rodgers knows better than to play with Sean Payton. H***, I ain’t even played for Sean Payton, and I know not to play with Sean.” Benching Nix and bringing in Rodgers, and the media frenzy he would drag to Denver with him, would certainly be a statement by the Broncos. Friday was, however, a huge opportunity for the Broncos to open up a gap on the Kansas City Chiefs following their loss to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. The Broncos need a much higher level from their quarterback if they are going to make any waves in the postseason. Whether Rodgers would offer that is an entirely different question, with the veteran having a lot more than just football on his mind right now after his Steelers saga. item.title: ‘They took this public’: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after locker room remarks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers has insisted that when his football career is over, he’ll go quietly into the background. However, after an ugly exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers, including a benching, a tell-all call on The Pat McAfee Show, and his subsequent release, Rodgers is making sure his voice is heard and that he has a say in the narrative. During Thursday’s call of the Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles game, Fox analyst and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady was critical of Aaron Rodgers calling into McAfee’s show to air out his grievances. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players,” Brady said. “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates. You’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say.” “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place” Tom Brady takes issue with how Aaron Rodgers handled his Steelers benching on Wednesday https://t.co/gRRpgcKo41 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 27, 2026 Rodgers’ former team hosted the Denver Broncos on Friday, and Rodgers made sure that he got the final word as far as “sanctity” goes. This time, Rodgers sent a text to Prime Video play-by-play man Al Michaels, who was on the call for Friday’s game. “Been the only story in town, of course, the Aaron Rodgers saga,” Michaels said during his broadcast of the Steelers’ 27-5 win over Denver. “Earlier today, I heard from Aaron, who said, he said, ‘A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room.’ “He said, ‘The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.’ He then also said, ‘They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leak at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That’s why I went to McAfee.” For his part, even as Rodgers does his best to control the narrative, Michaels feels that the quarterback’s legacy has taken a hit. If this is truly it for Rodgers, it was an ugly end to what was an extraordinary career. item.title: Matt Coronato’s Return to New York Brings Back Memories of a Rare Feat in Flames History
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Coronato scored his seventh goal of the season Friday against the New Jersey Devils, giving the Calgary Flames forward goals in back-to-back games heading into Saturday’s matchup against the New York Rangers. The Long Island native has a little more reason to look forward to playing at Madison Square Garden than most of his teammates, though. The last time Coronato made his way through all three NHL arenas in the New York area on the same road trip, he accomplished something only Jarome Iginla had done in Flames history. Coronato joined Iginla in the Flames’ record books The Flames were fighting for a playoff spot in March 2025 when they visited the Rangers, Devils and New York Islanders in a span of five days. Coronato entered the trip with 16 goals on the season and left with 20, helping the Flames collect all six available points. As FlamesNation’s Ryan Pike pointed out at the time , Coronato became just the second player in franchise history to score in all three New York-area arenas on the same road trip. Iginla was the first to do it in December 1999. Part of what makes the feat so rare is that Calgary had only played all three teams on the same road trip seven times since the Devils relocated to New Jersey in 1982. Coronato scored the game-winning goal on the power play against the Rangers on March 18, beating Igor Shesterkin from the slot. Two nights later, an attempted pass to Nazem Kadri deflected off Dawson Mercer’s stick and beat former Flames goaltender Jacob Markstrom. Coronato saved his best performance for the team he grew up cheering for, scoring twice against the Islanders on March 22. He opened the scoring just 36 seconds into the game before scoring his 20th goal of the season in the second period. The four goals accounted for 20% of Coronato’s production through that point in the season, and he did it in his first NHL appearances in all three buildings. While reaching the 20-goal mark for the first time in his career would’ve been special regardless of where it happened, doing it against his childhood team with family in the area made for a pretty memorable week. Coronato is finding his scoring touch again Coronato’s goal against New Jersey on Friday came after some good work below the goal line by Morgan Frost and Aydar Suniev, the latter of whom was one of two players Calgary received in the Tyler Toffoli trade . Coronato found some open ice in the slot and beat Jake Allen to tie the game at 2-2. The Flames forward is up to seven goals and 12 assists through Calgary’s first 27 games of the season. He’s been more productive as a playmaker than a goal scorer to this point, but Calgary invested $45.5 million in Coronato over seven years in large part because of his ability to put the puck in the net. Getting him going as a goal scorer would be a big help for a team that’s still trying to figure out where most of its offense will come from in the coming years. The schedule won’t give Corona

item.title: Greg Sankey Faces New Legal Trouble as LSU Dispute Takes Unexpected Turn
item.description: SEC commissioner Greg Sankey talks during a press conference before a celebration for OU joining the Southeastern Conference in Norman, Okla., Monday, July 1, 2024. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey is facing another serious development in his escalating dispute with LSU. However, this time, the controversy extends beyond his role as the conference’s commissioner. A newly amended lawsuit has placed Sankey himself at the center of a legal fight involving an LSU basketball player, with allegations that could carry personal financial consequences. The development comes just days before SEC university presidents and chancellors are scheduled to consider LSU’s future in the conference. Greg Sankey Personally Named in Amended Lawsuit Former LSU basketball player RJ Luis Jr. filed an amended lawsuit Wednesday, Nov. 25, naming Sankey as a defendant in both his official and personal capacities. According to reporting from Reuters and ESPN, Luis is seeking unspecified financial damages related to the SEC’s handling of his eligibility dispute. The filing also requests a jury trial. Luis’ attorneys allege that Sankey and the conference deliberately interfered with his opportunity to compete for LSU. They further contend that the commissioner acted with malice toward their client. Those claims remain allegations and have not been established in court. Nevertheless, the decision to name Sankey personally represents a significant escalation in the dispute. Lawsuit Alleges SEC Commissioner Threatened LSU The controversy centers on LSU’s decision to allow Luis to play basketball despite the SEC’s objections to his eligibility. Luis previously signed professional basketball contracts after his time at St. John’s. The SEC maintains eligibility standards restricting participation by athletes with certain professional experience. However, Luis obtained a Louisiana court injunction protecting his ability to compete without conference penalties. He subsequently made his LSU debut against Louisiana-Monroe on Nov. 18. Luis recorded 11 points and nine rebounds in 15 minutes. According to the amended lawsuit, Sankey communicated to LSU President Wade Rousse that the university could lose its SEC membership if Luis appeared in another game. The alleged communication occurred Nov. 19, one day after Luis’ debut. Rousse subsequently instructed LSU basketball coach Will Wade not to play Luis again. Luis’ attorneys argue that the conference’s actions effectively prevented their client from continuing his college basketball career. LSU Player Seeks Financial Damages The amended filing outlines several categories of alleged financial and personal harm. Luis is seeking compensation related to lost name, image and likeness opportunities, potential future earnings and damage to his professional prospects. His attorneys also cite alleged emotional distress and reputational harm. Additionally, the lawsuit seeks legal

item.title: Nations Championship finals weekend results, fixtures and hemisphere shield score
item.description: The inaugural Nations Championship has reached its climax with the finals weekend seeing six top-class international rugby matches across an action-packed three days at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham , with either South Africa or France set to be crowned the first-ever winner on Sunday evening The new competition has pitted the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows, with all 12 teams having had their seedings for this finals weekend determined by those results. The Springboks topped the southern hemisphere table, while France did likewise in the northern hemisphere standings, meaning those two heavyweights will clash for the title at 4.40pm GMT on Sunday – in a rematch of their incredible battle in Paris, narrowly won by Les Bleus , earlier this month – with the victors lifting the Nations Championship trophy. Before that, there will be five other matches across three days with each country facing their equivalent finisher from the group stage – including tantalising match-ups such as England against the All Blacks and Scotland v Argentina . Meanwhile the two hemispheres will also battle for the Hemisphere Shield in a ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system across the weekend. Here’s everything you need to know about finals weekend: Finals weekend results and fixtures - Allianz Stadium, Twickenham FRIDAY 27 NOVEMBER 6th vs 6th: Italy 23-21 Fiji 3rd vs 3rd: Ireland 38-14 Australia SATURDAY 28 NOVEMBER 5th vs 5th (1.10pm): Wales vs Japan 2nd vs 2nd (4.40pm): England vs New Zealand SUNDAY 29 NOVEMBER 4th vs 4th (1.10pm): Scotland vs Argentina 1st vs 1st – Nations Championship final (4.40pm): France vs South Africa What is the Hemisphere Shield? In addition to the Nations Championship itself, the Hemisphere Shield is also on offer as the northern hemisphere and southern hemisphere go head to head across the weekend. A ‘Ryder Cup-style’ points system will decide its fate with each victory in the matches featuring the second- to sixth-place finishers worth one point and victory in the Nations Championship final itself worth two points – meaning seven points are on offer and the first hemisphere to rack up four points will claim the Hemisphere Shield. In the event of a draw in the 6th vs 6th, 5th vs 5th, 4th vs 4th, 3rd vs 3rd or 2nd vs 2nd matches, the game will go to 10 minutes of golden point extra time (with the first team to score being declared the winners) and if neither side scores, each team will receive half a point towards the Hemisphere Shield. The final cannot end in a draw, so if the scores are still level after golden point extra time, then a place-kicking contest will occur to decide the champion.
