item.title: Alabama Faces Nightmare Iron Bowl Scenario That Could Change Its Entire Season
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer stands and looks down field during a time out against the Vanderbilt Commodores during the second half at FirstBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama enters Saturday’s Iron Bowl with one championship opportunity already gone. However, Auburn has an opportunity to deliver an even more painful blow to the Crimson Tide. The annual rivalry returns to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, with Alabama attempting to protect its College Football Playoff position. Meanwhile, Auburn has an opportunity to turn an otherwise disappointing season into an unforgettable one. And the Tigers could accomplish that by ruining their biggest rival’s postseason outlook. Alabama Already Received Bad News Before Iron Bowl Alabama entered rivalry weekend with an opportunity to reach the SEC Championship Game. However, the Crimson Tide needed help from other conference opponents. Texas’ victory over Texas A&M on Friday eliminated Alabama from the conference championship race. The Longhorns will face Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5. Consequently, Alabama must now pursue a national championship without another opportunity to improve its résumé in the SEC title game. That makes Saturday’s rivalry matchup especially important. A victory would allow Alabama to finish the regular season at 10-2. However, a loss would leave the Crimson Tide at 9-3 and introduce another layer of uncertainty into the playoff selection process. Auburn Could Deliver Alabama’s Worst-Case Scenario Auburn enters Saturday’s game at 7-4 following three consecutive victories. The Tigers most recently defeated Samford 59-17, producing one of their strongest offensive performances of the season. However, Saturday presents a considerably more difficult challenge. Alabama has won three consecutive games, outscoring those opponents by a combined 99-19. The Crimson Tide also enters the weekend ranked among the nation’s top College Football Playoff contenders. Nevertheless, the Iron Bowl has repeatedly demonstrated that records and expectations do not always determine the outcome. An Auburn victory would represent a major upset. More importantly, it would hand Alabama a third loss just before the playoff selection committee begins making its final decisions. Could Alabama Miss the College Football Playoff? Alabama currently holds a strong position in the playoff race. However, a third defeat could create significant uncertainty surrounding its postseason destination. The selection committee considers factors including overall record, strength of schedule, head-to-head results and performance against common opponents. Consequently, Alabama’s final ranking would depend partly on results elsewhere. A loss to Auburn would not automatically eliminate the Crimson Tide. However, it could place Alabama in a much more vulnerable position

item.title: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision
item.description: Celtics' Neemias Queta Could Force Difficult Mitchell Robinson Decision originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Celtics decided to make a move that seemed to be one of the more impressive of the offseason when they signed Mitchell Robinson, the former Knicks NBA champion. To say that Robinson's time in Boston has gone as planned would be wrong, as he's been very below average, to say the least. The Celtics, however, are very fortunate that some other players have stepped up in his struggles, including Neemias Queta. Queta, who hasn't always been a player who the Celtics can count on, has been with Boston since 2023-2024. Before the 2025-26 season, he had started in only six games in his entire career. Last year he started in 75, and this year he started in 12 of the 17 he's played. Queta is playing better than ever, putting up career highs in multiple statistics, including 10.4 points per game. But it also raises the question of what the Celtics could do with Robinson. If there is any possibility of moving on from Robinson, somebody like Queta playing at this level definitely helps. If the Celtics hadn't gotten this type of production out of the big man, they would find themselves in one of the more difficult positions in the NBA because of it. Instead, the Celtics now have a player they can trade in a couple of weeks and should still get a somewhat decent package. Robinson likely isn't going to return multiple draft picks or anything of that sort, but he shouldn't have to be salary dumped. item.title: Ben Roethlisberger gives his verdict on Mason Rudolph’s first start after Aaron Rodgers release
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to Aaron Rodgers in emphatic fashion. After a week in which Aaron Rodgers was benched, publicly flamed head coach Mike McCarthy, and was subsequently released by the team, the Steelers sent a message to the four-time MVP that they are just fine without him. They beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 with backup Mason Rudolph at quarterback, an immensely impressive display against a team that made the AFC Championship game last season. Steelers’ legendary quarterback Ben Roethlisberger shared his honest thoughts on the game afterward, including his verdict on Rudolph’s performance in his first start without Rodgers on the team. Ben Roethlisberger’s honest verdict on Mason Rudolph’s performance against the Broncos Roethlisberger won two Super Bowls as the Steelers’ quarterback, so who better to assess Rudolph’s performance? On his podcast, Footbahlin, he said he was impressed by the 31-year-old’s showing. Roethlisberger said, “I will give a lot of kudos and credit to Mason Rudolph. He got thrown into a crazy situation: hey, you are now the starter, we are going to bench a gold jacket Hall of Fame guy, and you are now taking his job.” “We talked about it all the time on the show, the best backups in the world—guys that I played with, like Rob Gronkowski, Byron [Leftwich], Charlie Batch, Joshua Dobbs, Duck [Hodges], and Jones. “They were always ready to go. You prepare yourself to play, but also prepare the team and the other quarterback to get ready to go. They literally, in as coach Tom [Tomlin] would say, the 11th hour, said, ‘Hey, here you go.’ “Going into this game against a Denver football team that was 8-2, at the top of the AFC, a really good football team. DK [Metcalf] is probably the biggest fan right now of Aaron [Rodgers] because they took all the pressure off of him. “Mason Rudolph stepped up tonight. Was he great? No, but he did not have to be great. He had to do what was effective enough that we got the win.” Rudolph was solid in his game against the Broncos, completing nine of his 15 pass attempts, throwing for 142 yards, throwing a touchdown, and no interceptions. It was all he needed to deliver, with an elite defense holding the Broncos to no touchdowns and scoring two of their own. If the Steelers’ defense performs to that level from here on out, all they need is clean football from Rudolph. item.title: Ole Miss hits Mississippi State with a familiar Egg Bowl celebration seven years later
item.description: The peeing-dog celebration made another Egg Bowl appearance Friday in Oxford, Mississippi, late in the Ole Miss Rebels’ 41-17 win over the Mississippi State Bulldogs. The latest version came from a Rebels defensive tackle, who lifted his right leg after Ole Miss scored to go up 40-17 with 1:57 left. The extra point that followed closed the scoring. Will Echoles, the tackle, was borrowing a move with two very different endings in this rivalry. In 2017, receiver DK Metcalf mimicked a dog after a touchdown against Mississippi State and drew a penalty in a game Ole Miss won 31-28. In 2019, Elijah Moore did it after a 2-yard touchdown catch with four seconds left that pulled the Rebels within 21-20. Ole Miss hits a pee celebration in the Egg Bowl against Mississippi State. (via ABC) https://t.co/hxRx2MNexH — On3 (@On3) November 27, 2026 Jan 8, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2026 Fiesta Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Moore’s celebration drew a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty that pushed the tying extra point back to 35 yards. Luke Logan missed it wide right, Mississippi State won 21-20, and Moore issued an apology the next day. “I apologize to my teammates, coaches and Rebel Nation for my actions at the end of the game. It was an emotional moment, and I deeply regret it. It does not represent who I am or who we are as a team, and I will grow stronger from this mistake,” Moore said in a statement. Coach Matt Luke and athletic director Keith Carter followed with a joint statement calling the celebration “disappointing and unacceptable.” Ole Miss has now won four straight Egg Bowls Echoles struck the pose after Ole Miss had turned a 10-6 halftime deficit into a rout, outscoring the Bulldogs 35-7 after the break. The Rebels led only 20-17 entering the fourth quarter, then scored the final 21 points, with Joshua Dye’s 1-yard run setting up the celebration. Fluff Bothwell ran for 129 yards on 18 carries for Mississippi State, and his 16-yard touchdown run in the second quarter gave the Bulldogs their first lead in an SEC game since Week 4 against the Missouri Tigers. Trinidad Chambliss completed 23 of 36 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another score. The win was the Rebels’ fourth in a row in the series and their sixth in the last seven meetings. The loss left Mississippi State at 5-7 for a second straight season and kept coach Jeff Lebby winless against Ole Miss in three tries. Pete Golding’s Rebels finished the regular season 8-4 and are waiting on their bowl assignment. Moore’s flag came with four seconds left in a one-point game. Echoles picked a 23-point lead and under two minutes to play, about as safe a moment as the Egg Bowl offers for that particular pose. item.title: Urban Meyer gives common sense recommendation to USC’s Lincoln Riley ahead of UCLA game
item.description: The USC Trojans close the regular season Saturday against the UCLA Bruins with an 8-3 record, and losses to the Oregon Ducks, Wisconsin Badgers and Indiana Hoosiers have kept Lincoln Riley’s fifth season in Los Angeles under steady scrutiny. Urban Meyer, the former Ohio State coach who now works as a Fox Sports analyst, laid out what he would do about Riley on this week’s episode of The Triple Option, the podcast he hosts with Rob Stone and Mark Ingram II. Jan 20, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Urban Meyer looks on during the second half the CFP National Championship college football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things,” Meyer said. URBAN MEYER WEIGHS IN: Former national championship-winning head coach and FOX Sports analyst Urban Meyer weighed in on the future of #USC HC Lincoln Riley during an appearance on The Triple Option Show. Meyer believes USC possesses one of the most talented rosters in the Big Ten but acknowledged that the Trojans don’t consistently perform up to their potential. “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way.” Despite USC’s inconsistencies, Meyer doesn’t believe the Trojans should move on from Riley. Instead, he believes Riley needs to hire an offensive coordinator and become more involved in overseeing every aspect of the program. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things.” Meyer’s comments raise an interesting question surrounding the structure of USC’s coaching staff and whether Riley’s responsibilities as an offensive play-caller are limiting his effectiveness as a head coach. Five seasons into the Lincoln Riley era, is it time for Riley to relinquish offensive play-calling duties? : Icon Sportswire — Trojans Zone (@TrojansZone) November 27, 2026 Luke Huard is in his second season as USC’s offensive coordinator , with Riley calling the plays, so the hire Meyer described would mean handing the play sheet to someone else. Riley hired Gary Patterson, who led TCU for 21 seasons and was named to the College Football Hall of Fame class of 2026, to run the defense this season. “I’m certainly feeling his impact of just having a fellow head coach in the building, somebody else that has sat in this chair and make some of these decisions,” Riley said at Big Ten media days in July. item.title: Serie A Preview: Como vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Como vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is the venue as Como and Juventus go head-to-head in a standout Serie A fixture on Sunday evening. Both sides head into proceedings amid a rich vein of form, looking to consolidate their respective positions in the league standings. Cesc Fabregas’ side have enjoyed an outstanding start to the campaign, collecting 26 points from their opening 12 matches and establishing a five-point cushion over the Bianconeri. Juventus arrive in Lombardy in improved form after recording consecutive victories across all competitions. However, Luciano Spalletti’s men face a stern examination against a side that have proved particularly difficult to beat on home soil. Match Preview Como Como continued their impressive European campaign with a 1-0 victory over AEK Athens on Tuesday. Luis Milla scored the decisive goal at the start of the second half, securing a fourth win in five Champions League outings and keeping the Lariani firmly on course for the knockout stages. Fabregas’ side have also maintained their momentum in Serie A, where they sit fifth, only a point adrift of fourth-placed Milan. They bounced back from their defeat to Inter by beating Cagliari 2-0 last weekend, with Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha finding the net. The hosts have won eight of their opening 12 league fixtures (D2, L2) and boast one of the division’s strongest defensive records. They have conceded just 10 goals, while their home form has been particularly impressive, with four victories and one draw from five matches. Como have also kept four consecutive clean sheets at the Sinigaglia, against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia, and Cagliari. Another positive result would open up an eight-point gap over Juventus and strengthen their position in a fiercely contested top-four race. The Lariani also have fond recent memories of this fixture, having beaten Juventus 2-0 in both league meetings last season. They had not defeated the Turin giants at home in Serie A since 1952 before ending that long wait in October 2025. Juventus Juventus have gradually rediscovered their attacking confidence under Spalletti, winning their last two games across all competitions. After thrashing Venezia 4-0 in Serie A, the Bianconeri came from behind to defeat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 in the Europa League on Thursday. The Turin giants have now scored 14 goals in their last five outings, suggesting their attacking problems may finally be easing. However, their domestic campaign remains inconsistent, with six wins, three draws and three defeats leaving them sixth in the standings on 21 points. Juventus have also stuttered away from home, which spells trouble ahead of this showdown. They have secured only two victories from six Serie A trips this season (D2, L2), scoring eight goals and conceding the same number. Their defensive record nevertheless offers encouragement. item.title: Former Georgia Star Makes Stunning Rivalry Admission Before Bulldogs Face Georgia Tech
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) hands the ball off to Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) during the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia football is preparing to make history against Georgia Tech on Saturday, but one former Bulldogs standout will find himself in an unusual position. His son is playing for the other team. Former Georgia running back Verron Haynes, who once delivered a memorable performance against the Yellow Jackets, will be supporting Georgia Tech as his son, Justice Haynes, attempts to upset the nation’s No. 1 team. The family connection adds another fascinating storyline to a rivalry already filled with bad blood. And this time, Georgia’s history is directly involved. Former Georgia Standout Faces Unusual Rivalry Decision Verron Haynes played for Georgia from 1999 through 2001, establishing himself as a productive running back before beginning his professional career. His most memorable performance against Georgia Tech came in 2001. Haynes rushed for 207 yards on 39 carries, helping the Bulldogs secure a victory over their in-state rivals. More than two decades later, his son is preparing to face Georgia from the opposite sideline. Justice Haynes, who previously played at Alabama and Michigan, now represents Georgia Tech. The running back also has strong family connections to Athens. Both of his parents attended Georgia, making Saturday’s matchup particularly personal. Justice Haynes Reveals Where His Father’s Loyalty Stands Despite his family’s Georgia background, Justice Haynes made it clear that his father will support him Saturday. Speaking to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Haynes explained that his parents have supported his football journey regardless of the program he represents. He also revealed that his father plans to wear Georgia Tech colors for the rivalry game. The admission provides an unusual twist to one of the South’s oldest college football rivalries. A former Georgia star who once helped defeat Georgia Tech will now be cheering for the Yellow Jackets. However, the decision reflects family loyalty rather than any publicly stated disagreement with Georgia. Justice has consistently emphasized the support he receives from his parents. Georgia Tech Has Opportunity to Ruin Bulldogs’ Historic Moment Saturday’s matchup carries additional significance for Georgia. The Bulldogs have defeated Georgia Tech in eight consecutive meetings, matching the longest winning streak in series history. Georgia Tech previously won eight straight games from 1949 through 1956. Now, Kirby Smart’s program has an opportunity to establish a new record with a ninth consecutive victory. However, the Yellow Jackets would love nothing more than to prevent that milestone. item.title: Low turnout, BVAS glitches mar INEC mock accreditation in Ondo
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure The ongoing mock accreditation and voting exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections has recorded low voter turnout in some polling units in Ondo State, alongside technical challenges with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). As of the time of filing this report, findings showed that only two persons voted out of 470 registered voters at Tipper Garage, Ward 2, Unit 046. Similarly, at Champion Junction, Ward 3, Unit 15, only six voters participated in the exercise. At High Court, Ward 5, Unit 11, 11 persons were recorded as having voted out of 940 registered voters. However, the situation was different at Ajipowo, Ward 2, Unit 17, where a large turnout of voters was observed. Despite the turnout, the exercise experienced technical challenges as the BVAS reportedly failed to capture the faces of some elderly voters, causing difficulties during the accreditation process. The mock exercise is part of INEC’s preparations to test its electoral equipment and processes ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. Comparing the policy with the restrictions under previous military administrations, Akande said individuals were previously prevented from generating electricity independently. “Unlike what the military did before, if you tried to create electricity, they would arrest you. They would make you a debtor. They wouldn’t let you do it. They said only the Federal Government could do it. Tinubu came and said everybody can do it,” he added. On his own public engagements, the former governor attributed his reduced movement around the country to age, contrasting his present situation with when he was younger. item.title: Low voter turnout mars INEC mock election in Bayelsa, as accreditation process runs smoothly
item.description: •Reports across the state indicate a seamless exercise despite poor participation By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The mock election organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) recorded a low voter turnout across Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, on Saturday, despite reports of a smooth accreditation process. The exercise, designed to test the commission’s preparedness and assess the performance of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections, was seamless at the polling units visited. At the Kpansia Epie Community Town Hall, no fewer than nine voters had completed the accreditation process as of 11:15 a.m. when this reporter left the unit. The Assistant Presiding Officer, Sampson Wale, confirmed that operations with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) were seamless. The story is not different at Epie II CPS Opolo II and others. The BVAS is being tested as part of efforts to identify and address possible challenges before the general elections. Though participation was relatively low, INEC officials expressed optimism that voter turnout would improve as the exercise progressed. Reports from other parts of the state also described the mock exercise as smooth. item.title: 2026 Kindle Paperwhite review: Page-turn buttons are back, for a price
item.description: Supply pressures, shortages, and inflation have pushed tech prices relentlessly upward over the last half-decade, and even basic gadgets haven't been immune. That's why you can spend $385 on a Raspberry Pi, or why the cheapest Amazon Kindle in 2026 costs more than the midrange one from a few years ago . "New thing, better features, same price" used to be a reliable formula, but now you're lucky if you can get the same thing for barely more than before. The 2024 Kindles all came with small price increases, but the 2026 models make them look like stellar deals. The $160 Kindle Paperwhite from two years ago wipes the floor with this year's $150 Kindle in just about every conceivable way, from screen size to front light quality to waterproofing—something to consider if you're choosing between a used or refurbished Paperwhite and one of these new models. The flagship of the now five-model-large monochrome Kindle family is the $250 2026 Paperwhite Signature Edition, which takes the core specs of the new $200 Paperwhite and puts it in a sturdy iPad-esque aluminum case instead of the typical plastic. item.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. item.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
item.description: A dozen grains of dust that have wandered in from the distant Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune were found floating in Earth's stratosphere. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system. When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago. If there is a reservoir of heavy water out in the solar system's hinterlands, understanding how that water got out there and stayed out there will inform models that describe the growth of the planets. Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and an oxygen atom. What we usually refer to as heavy water is water that contains a heavy isotope of hydrogen. An isotope is an atom that contains the usual number of protons for that element, but a different number of neutrons . Elements are determined by the number of protons they contain. For example, hydrogen always has just one proton. Ordinary 'light' hydrogen has 1 proton and no neutrons, but its heavy isotopes – deuterium and tritium – contain 1 and 2 neutrons, respectively, in addition to the proton. However, there's another kind of water that features heavy isotopes of oxygen instead. Ordinary 'light' oxygen is made from 8 protons and 8 neutrons and is hence known as oxygen-16 but some oxygen isotopes can have 9 or 10 neutrons, and we call these isotopes oxygen-17 or -18. There have been a few clues that such a reservoir exists. Mineralogical evidence from a single carbonaceous chondritic meteorite and measurements from comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko indicated the presence of minerals that had formed from interactions between silicate rock and abundant oxygen-heavy variety of water, but it was not clear whether these were isolated instances or a clue to something more widespread. An illustration comparing the locations of the solar system planets to the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud, a theorized shell of icy objects at the farthest reaches of our solar system. (Image credit: ESA) Another data point comes from NASA's Genesis mission, which launched in 2001 and collected particles from the solar wind that were subsequently returned to Earth for study. The analysis of these particles indicated that the sun contains proportionally more ordinary 'light' oxygen than Earth and most meteorites. This suggests that there could be an outwards gradient of increasing abundance of heavy oxygen. Yet the Kuiper Belt is so far away that it makes finding more evidence for this difficult. However, rather than having to go to the Kuiper Belt to sample the water-ice there, dust grains can bring a little bit of the Kuiper Belt to us. T

item.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
item.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. The post Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
item.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. The post UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027. He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities. Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State. He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation. Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country. On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children. According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction. On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually. He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements. On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for individuals living with disabilities. He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities. Adebayo endorsed the SDP governorship candidate in the state, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, saying his experience in policing would be an asset in addressing security challenges. He urged voters to assess political candidates based on their records, character and policy proposals rather than party affiliations. The presidential candidate also called for an enabling environment for opposition parties to participate in the electoral process, stressing the importance of political competition in a democracy. item.title: Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku & By Dennis Agbo Linc Edochie, the third son of the late Pete Edochie, could not hold back his tears when he saw his father’s corpse in the mortuary. The movie legend died in the early hours of Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. He had taken ill and was rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he passed away. Painting a gloomy picture of the atmosphere at the late actor’s riverside residence in Trans-Ekulu, Enugu-based actor and filmmaker, Steve Eboh, said Linc broke down the moment he sighted his father’s body. “When Linc stormed the mortuary and sighted his father’s corpse, he cried profusely and leaned on his brother’s shoulder. We consoled him and prayed for the family,” Eboh said. Eboh added that grief was written all over the faces of people whose lives Pete Edochie had touched during his acting career. “We thank God for a life well spent. He was a legend who touched so many lives. He was not just an actor, he was a global icon. Everybody knew him.” Our correspondent, who visited the late actor’s Trans-Ekulu residence, described a gloomy picture of desertion and sorrow. “Apart from a domestic aide seen at the premises, there was little indication of the tragic development that had thrown the family and the Nigerian entertainment industry into mourning,” he noted. A source familiar with the circumstances surrounding his death told our correspondent that the actor took ill on Tuesday night and was subsequently rushed to a hospital in Enugu, where he died at about 12:30am on Wednesday. According to the source, Edochie’s family had remained at the hospital since his death, apparently attending to necessary arrangements and coming to terms with the loss. The family’s absence from the residence accounted for the quiet atmosphere observed during the reporter’s visit. The post Pete Edochie: Linc breaks down in tears as unusual calm rules Enugu residence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Peedi Picasso, CEO of Aristokrat Records, has opened up on why he refused to renew Burna Boy’s record deal, saying the singer demanded an 85-15 per cent revenue split in his favour. Picasso, whose real name is Piriye Isokrari said their previous deal gave Burna Boy 60 per cent, while the label took 40 per cent. He also revealed that the singer’s mother insisted he should only sign two-year contracts, a condition that influenced the label’s decision. According to Picasso, the proposed increase did not make financial sense at the time because the label was not making significant money from record sales. Picasso said live performances and endorsement deals were the major sources of revenue. He argued that accepting an 80-20 or 85-15 split would have left the label with a smaller share of the income despite the money it was investing in the singer. Picasso said the arrangement was difficult to justify for another two-year contract, particularly because the label was not entering a long-term deal. However, he admitted that his position has changed, saying he would now accept the terms he previously rejected. “Today I will take the 85/15 per cent now, but back then, it didn’t make any sense,” he said. He also explained that Burna Boy received the larger share of performance earnings under their former agreement because he was the artiste taking the stage. The post Why I turned down Burna Boy’s 85/15 demand – Aristokrat boss, Peedi Picasso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation
item.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. As at the time of filing this report, at exactly 9:29 am , officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission were yet to be on ground to commence the exercise scheduled to commence by 8:3am. The only security presence observed is that of three personnel of the Nigeria Security CIVIL Defence Corps (NSCDC) There is also no presence of voters at the two polling units, raising questions about the level of preparedness and awareness ahead of the exercise. The situation contrasts with INEC’s earlier assurance of readiness for the mock election, which is designed to assess its operational capacity and the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result transmission technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. As at Friday night, when voting materials were distributed at the INEC office in Kaduna, the Administrative Secretary, Abba Yahaya, also assured the public of the Commission’s readiness for the mock election, expressing confidence in its preparedness to conduct the exercise. The exercise is expected to simulate the 2027 Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The situation is, however, slightly different at polling unit 002, located within Narayi Primary School, also in Chikun Local Government Area. As of 10 a.m., some voters were seen hanging around the polling area, awaiting the commencement of the exercise. However, as at the time of this report, INEC officials were yet to arrive, leaving the voters waiting without any indication of when the mock election would begin. The post Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Lawal pledges more projects as APC Campaign visits Shinkafi
item.description: Governor seeks support for Tinubu, APC candidates ahead of 2027 polls Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has pledged to execute more development projects in Shinkafi Local Government Area as he canvassed support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. Lawal made the pledge on Friday during the APC Zamfara North campaign flag-off rally held at the Eid ground in Shinkafi. The rally attracted party chieftains, including the Director-General of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council and former governor, Abdul’aziz Yari; another former governor, Mahmuda Aliyu Shinkafi; the state APC Chairman, Kabiru Moyi; and other party leaders. Tens of thousands of supporters reportedly welcomed the campaign entourage at the town’s entrance, chanting slogans in support of the party. Addressing the gathering, Lawal thanked the people of Shinkafi for their solidarity and warm reception, saying their support was encouraging. He said his administration had recorded achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic development. The governor disclosed that his administration had rehabilitated six primary healthcare centres, including facilities in Badarawa, Birnin Yero, Galadi, Jangeru and Kurya. He described the ongoing referral hospital project in Shinkafi as a legacy initiative that would transform healthcare delivery in Zamfara State and the North-West. According to him, the project is central to his administration’s commitment to improving access to quality healthcare. Lawal also said his administration had completed 22 of the 31 projects undertaken over the past three and a half years, while the remaining nine were at more than 80 per cent completion. He urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu, his administration and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. “I am here once again to seek your votes. Vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, vote for me, and vote for the APC from top to bottom in the upcoming 2027 general election,” he said. The governor’s spokesman, Sulaiman Bala Idris, disclosed this in a statement issued on November 27, 2026. item.title: Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso admitted Chelsea are in a “difficult moment” as the beleaguered boss urged his struggling side to stick together after their dismal 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest on Friday. Alonso’s side crashed to a third successive Premier League loss to leave them languishing in eighth place. The Blues have lost four of their last five league matches, piling pressure on Alonso just months into his reign at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea fell behind to Igor Jesus’s early opener before Morgan Gibbs-White doubled Forest’s lead with a second half penalty. Emmanuel Emegha reduced the deficit but Gibbs-White struck again to make Emega’s late second nothing more than a footnote on another dispiriting evening for Alonso. “It’s a difficult moment for everyone. It’s disappointing again to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions, we can’t stop,” Alonso said. “We are low in confidence, the team is struggling to hold a result. After getting to 2-1 we have conceded and go to 3-1. “Everything is not going our way, we are responsible for that and we are responsible to find solutions.” Chelsea have already conceded 23 goals in 12 league matches and their porous defence was not helped by Alonso’s curious decision to use Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo in a back-three. Alonso also selected Wesley Fofana after the centre-back was forced to apologise for joking in a YouTube interview about missing a penalty during Chelsea’s League Cup defeat against Liverpool this season. The hapless Fofana was booed by angry Chelsea fans at the City Ground and conceded a penalty with his careless foul on former Blues striker Liam Delap. “We need to support everyone. Everyone that is in the team we need to support,” Alonso said of Fofana. “We know we have to go through difficult moments. We don’t take apart anyone and we want to help.” Asked to assess Chelsea’s dismal run, Alonso suggested the only cure was hard work on the training ground. “We can do better for sure. At this level you need to hold results and that is why we are losing in the last games,” he said after Chelsea’s sixth league defeat his term. “That is the only way I understand football. When things are not going well, try to work and find solutions. It can happen that we turn it around and it goes our way.” Chelsea’s sixth league defeat under Alonso will spark pointed questions about the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. Although Alonso led Leverkusen to an historic Bundesliga title in 2024, he lasted just seven months before being sacked by Real. The former Liverpool midfielder desperately needs a win against bottom of the table Crystal Palace on Wednesday to avoid the sack talk growing even louder. “Everyone needs to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it,” he said. The post Chelsea in a ‘difficult moment’ admits Alonso appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment. The institution has developed specialised workshops, laboratories and practical tra

item.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
item.description: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

item.title: The M5 MacBook Air just got its biggest discount since Apple raised the price
item.description: The M5-powered MacBook Air is $300 off in both size configurations for Black Friday. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge If you’ve been holding off on buying a new MacBook Air since Apple raised prices by $200 in June , you’re in luck. The 13-inch M5 MacBook Air is on sale at Amazon and Best Buy with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage starting at $999 ($300 off) for Black Friday, which is the lowest price we’ve seen since the hike. If you want a larger display, Amazon and Best Buy are also taking $300 off the otherwise identical 15-inch model with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, dropping it to $1,199. Apple MacBook Air 13 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $999 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $999 at Best Buy (512GB) $1599 $1199 at Amazon (1TB) Apple MacBook Air 15 (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $1199 at Amazon (512GB) $1299 $1199 at Best Buy (512GB) $1799 $1499 at Amazon (1TB) The M5-equipped MacBook Air is a good middle ground if you need more power than the MacBook Neo — which, thanks to a $100 discount , is $599 — but don’t want to splurge on a MacBook Pro. Its faster chip, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage make it better suited for multitasking and creative work in apps like Photoshop and Premiere. You also get a higher-resolution display, better speakers, a backlit keyboard that makes typing in the dark easier, and faster ports. Plus, its sharper webcam supports Apple’s Center Stage feature, which automatically adjusts the framing to keep you in view during video calls. Of course, the Air can’t match the performance or higher-end displays you can get with a MacBook Pro, whether you opt for an M5 model , the newer M5 Pro model with a PROLED XDR Display , or one of the M6-powered machines . A Pro may be worth the extra money if you regularly edit video or work on more demanding creative projects. But if you mostly need a laptop for work, browsing, and occasional photo or video editing, the M5 Air is more than capable. Read our M5-powered MacBook Air review .

item.title: The best Black Friday deals you can still get on AirPods, Macs, and other Apple gear
item.description: The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR has hit a new low price just a few months after release. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , too, which are available at their lowest prices to date. In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review . The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy , which is $19 shy of their best price to date ( Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review . Beats Studio Pro The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. item.title: Sony’s 1000XM4C headphones are a Black Friday bargain at $198
item.description: The fan-favorite folding design returns with the comfortable, slightly improved XM4C headphones. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart . That’s $100 off their October launch price. Sony WH-1000XM4C Where to Buy: $299.99 $198 at Amazon $299.99 $198 at Walmart $299.99 $199.99 at Best Buy There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up. These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027. Read our Sony WH-1000XM4C review .

item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: I captured images of my first-ever solar eclipse with the Unistellar Equinox 2 — now 20% off for Black Friday
item.description:
Harry joined Space.com in December 2024 as an e-commerce staff writer covering cameras, optics, and skywatching content. Based in the UK, Harry graduated in 2019 with a Bachelor's degree in American Literature with Creative Writing from the University of East Anglia. A keen photographer, Harry has strong experience with astrophotography and has captured celestial objects with a range of cameras. item.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash. The FBI on Oct. 31 published

item.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. item.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
item.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern ha

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
item.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .
